prompt: Which movie features the line "I'll be back"?
funFact: Schwarzenegger lobbied to say "I will be back" — he thought the contraction sounded weak.

prompt: In Finding Nemo, what kind of fish is Dory?
funFact: After the film, demand for blue tangs spiked so hard that marine biologists issued warnings.

prompt: Which school does Harry Potter attend?
funFact: Durmstrang and Beauxbatons arrive in the fourth book; the American school was invented years later.

prompt: What is Luke Skywalker's home planet?
funFact: Its desert scenes were shot in Tunisia, where a real town called Tataouine lent the name.

prompt: Which animated film features a snowman named Olaf?
funFact: Olaf was rewritten late in production; an earlier version of him was the villain’s sidekick.

prompt: In Jurassic Park, which animals are brought back to life?
funFact: Only fifteen minutes of the film contain dinosaurs, and barely six of those are computer-generated.

prompt: Which superhero is also known as the Dark Knight?
funFact: His creators briefly gave him blond hair and a red suit before settling on the bat.

prompt: Who plays Captain Jack Sparrow?
funFact: The studio panicked at the performance and asked whether the character was meant to be drunk.

prompt: Which sitcom is set around a coffee shop called Central Perk?
funFact: The orange sofa was found in the studio basement, not bought — it had been in storage for years.

prompt: In The Lion King, what is Simba's father called?
funFact: Simba is simply Swahili for "lion" — several of the film's names come straight out of the language.

prompt: Which series is set at the Dunder Mifflin Paper Company?
funFact: The US version was adapted from a UK original that ran only 14 episodes.

prompt: Who directed both Inception and Oppenheimer?
funFact: Nolan famously avoids using a smartphone or email.

prompt: Who directed Pulp Fiction?
funFact: He wrote it while living in Amsterdam, which is why a character opens the film talking about it.

prompt: Which studio made Toy Story?
funFact: It was the first feature film animated entirely on computers, and it nearly got cancelled midway.

prompt: Who directed the 1979 film Alien?
funFact: The sequel went to James Cameron, who pitched it by writing "ALIEN" and adding an S as a dollar sign.

prompt: Which actor plays Tony Stark in the Marvel films?
funFact: The studio resisted for months; the director fought for him, then let him improvise most of the dialogue.

prompt: Who directed The Grand Budapest Hotel?
funFact: The hotel exterior is a model, filmed outdoors so the daylight on it would look real.

prompt: Which series follows the Crawley family at an English country estate?
funFact: The house is a real one, and its owners still live in a private wing while filming goes on.

prompt: Who directed Spirited Away?
funFact: He has announced his retirement at least five separate times and gone back to work after each.

prompt: Which studio's logo is a mountain ringed by stars?
funFact: The founder sketched it from memory of a mountain near his childhood home in Utah.

prompt: Which show's 1983 finale drew over 105 million US viewers?
funFact: It held the record for most-watched broadcast until the 2010 Super Bowl.

prompt: What is the highest-grossing film of all time (unadjusted)?
funFact: Avatar lost the crown to Endgame in 2019, then re-releases in China put it back on top.

prompt: Which film was the first non-English winner of Best Picture?
funFact: It won in 2020, ninety-two ceremonies in — and took Director, Screenplay and International Feature too.

prompt: Blade Runner was adapted from a novel by which author?
funFact: He died months before release, having seen only twenty minutes of test footage.

prompt: How many Academy Awards did Titanic win?
funFact: Only two other films have matched that total, and no film has ever beaten it.

prompt: Which actor has won the most Best Actor Oscars?
funFact: He took three, and between two of them he left acting entirely to train as a shoemaker.

prompt: Which Star Wars film reached cinemas first?
funFact: It carried no episode number in 1977; the "Episode IV" crawl was added for a re-release.

prompt: The film Jaws was based on a novel by whom?
funFact: He spent his later years campaigning for shark conservation, saying he regretted the panic.

prompt: Which film franchise features the character Ethan Hunt?
funFact: The first five instalments each had a different director, which is rare for a series that long.

prompt: In which year was the first Academy Awards ceremony held?
funFact: It lasted fifteen minutes, the winners were announced three months early, and tickets cost five dollars.

prompt: Which 1927 film won the first Academy Award for Best Picture?
funFact: Wings is the only fully silent film ever to win Best Picture.

prompt: In The Matrix, how is Neo first told to "follow the white rabbit"?
funFact: Seconds later, a rabbit tattoo appears at his door — the film's first big reality glitch.

prompt: In Jaws, the mechanical shark was nicknamed…
funFact: It broke down so often that the shark is barely shown, which is why the film is frightening.

prompt: Who was originally cast as Marty McFly in Back to the Future?
funFact: He shot for over a month before being replaced, and a few of his takes survive in the finished film.

prompt: Indiana Jones shoots the swordsman in Raiders because Harrison Ford was…
funFact: The scripted fight would have taken three days; he suggested the gun so he could go back to bed.

prompt: The Wilhelm scream was first heard in a film of which decade?
funFact: It has since been dropped into hundreds of films, usually as a private joke between sound editors.

prompt: What was the blood in the Psycho shower scene?
funFact: The film was shot in black and white, so what mattered was how it ran, not what colour it was.

prompt: Which actor turned down the role of Neo in The Matrix?
funFact: He made Wild Wild West instead, and has said publicly that he would have ruined the part.

prompt: The horse head in The Godfather was…
funFact: It came from a dog-food plant, and the actor was not told what would be under the sheet.

prompt: Which film was the first released with a Dolby Digital soundtrack?
funFact: The data was printed in the gaps between the sprocket holes, on film that also carried the old analogue track.
